messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: RDMA error spike detected in cluster us-west-2 serving pool. 5xx rate > 6% over 2m, multiple containers restarted. Paging oncall. Severity: P2 :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): seeing large number of CUDA OOM and container restarts on nodes rack-usw2-07-*. kernels show repeated 'mlx5_core' link resets. Logs: many 'gdr: transport reset' and 'ib_cm: QP error' entries.

jake (infra): on it. can you paste a sample pod log and the node names?

maria (oncall): pasted below:
```
kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide | grep model-serve
model-serve-1   CrashLoopBackOff   2/3   10d   10.0.7.12   rack-usw2-07-02
model-serve-2   Running           1/3   10d   10.0.7.13   rack-usw2-07-05
```

maria (oncall): tail from model-serve-1:
```
[2026-03-15T01:02:34Z] runtime: CUDA OOM allocating 512MB
[2026-03-15T01:02:35Z] serving: failed to fetch kvcache shard: rpc error: code = Unavailable
[2026-03-15T01:02:36Z] container: exiting with status 137
```

anita (sre): are the OOMs correlated with sudden RDMA packet loss or packet reorders? last incident had similar pattern.

nate (runtime): yes, KV cache RPCs spike with retransmits; when ib link goes bad we get longer tail latency that fills GPU memory with inflight KV pulls, causing OOMs and restarts. suspect intermittent packet loss on PF to PF.

colin (network): running ibstat on rack-usw2-07-02 now. output: 'link_layer: InfiniBand', 'phys_state: PORT_DOWN' for port 1 intermittently. Also seeing 'rx_errors' increment on mlx5.

jake (infra): can we repro with iftop or tcpdump on host? i'll spawn packet capture on the NIC and mirror to S3.

maria (oncall): starting mitigations: 1) reduce serving concurrency to 1 on affected pool, 2) scale down batch size via runtime feature flag, 3) enable CPU-fallback for critical models. Applying now.

nate (runtime): patching config:
```
PATCH /v1/configs/pool/us-west-2
{"concurrency":1,"max_batch_tokens":256,"fallback_policy":"cpu_quant_v1"}
```

maria (oncall): applied. immediate drop in 5xx to 3.1% but not back to baseline. requests with >200ms spikes still failing.

anita (sre): good. we should cordon the most flappy nodes and shift traffic away. recommend cordon rack-usw2-07-02 and 07-05, drain gracefully. @jake can you handle?

jake (infra): cordoning and draining 07-02 now. kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node/rack-usw2-07-02

jake (infra): drain completed for 07-02, some pods rescheduled to rack-usw2-03. CPU-fallback handled by rollout.

colin (network): opened ticket with colo ops: 'Intermittent port down on ToR -> mlx5 port flaps on rack-usw2-07'. They've acknowledged and said they'll inspect optics and replace a cable if needed. ETA 60m.

maria (oncall): customer impact assessment: approx 4% of inference requests in us-west-2 experienced 5xx or timeout between 01:00-01:10 UTC. Affected customers: 3 high-volume tenants saw transient rate increases; we're throttling traffic and routing as mitigation.

pager-duty-bot: Incident annotated: Escalation to hardware-team at 01:06, page sent.

nate (runtime): aside: the runtime's KV retry backoff currently allows up to 12 concurrent in-flight pulls per model shard. with packet loss that multiplies memory pressure. lowering to 4 reduces OOM risk. proposing immediate config change.

maria (oncall): go ahead and apply that change, nate. we'll monitor memory.

nate (runtime): applied: kv_inflight_per_shard=4. initial observa: per-node GPU mem headroom up ~20MB.

anita (sre): let's prepare a status page blurb in case colo ETA slips. Draft: "We are investigating increased inference errors in us-west-2 caused by network instability between hosts. Mitigations in progress; some requests may be slower or return errors. No data exposure."

maria (oncall): LGTM. posting in 10m if no further improvement.

colin (network): temporary workaround from colo: move affected hosts off ToR port 1 to port 3 (spare) while they inspect optics. scheduling cutover now - a 2m maintenance per host.

jake (infra): performing NIC rebind on rack-usw2-07-02: sudo ifdown eno1 && ifup eno1 and reloading mlx5 module: sudo modprobe -r mlx5_core && sudo modprobe mlx5_core.

maria (oncall): after NIC rebind, node came back with port UP and rx_errors stopped increasing. GPU OOMs reduced to single-digit over next 5m.

colin (network): colo confirmed a marginal SFP transceiver; replacing SFP on ToR. They expect full stability after replacement.

anita (sre): next steps: 1) keep reduced concurrency for 30m, 2) keep kv_inflight_per_shard at 4 for 60m, 3) schedule full canary re-enable after 60m with slow ramp.

maria (oncall): handing off oncall to jake at 01:33 UTC for night monitoring; I'll update incident timeline and put notes in pager log. @jake please ack when you take over.

jake (infra): ack. I'll monitor metrics and coordinate with colo if any recurrences. setting an alert to reopen pager if 5xx > 3% for 5m.

maria (oncall): incident status: mitigated -> partial service restored. customer impact: transient errors for ~4% requests, majority rerouted or served via CPU-fallback. Root cause suspected intermittent ToR SFP/transceiver causing RDMA packet loss and mlx5 resets leading to cascading GPU OOMs.

incident-bot: Incident updated: state=mitigated, severity=P2, assignees=[jake (infra)], timeline_url=https://redwood.internal/incidents/2165432100

jake (infra): leaving a short runbook note: if RDMA flaps observed -> 1) set pool concurrency to 1, 2) set kv_inflight_per_shard=4, 3) enable cpu_fallback, 4) cordon/drain flappy nodes, 5) contact colo for optics replacement. saving to /runbooks/rdma-flap.json.

maria (oncall): thanks team. closing primary pager; will re-open if colo reports any remaining instability. :thumbsup:
